slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A transformation is a rule that moves every point of the plane to an image point. We write A maps to A' (read "A prime").

The figure you start with is the preimage; the result is the image. A rigid motion (isometry) keeps every distance the same: translations, reflections and rotations are rigid motions. A transformation moves every point of the plane, not just the shape drawn on it.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Under a transformation, does a point that is not on the shape move?
slides.reveal: Yes, every point of the plane has an image. The shape just shows us some of them.
